question: Where must a School Speed Limit assembly be placed, what advance sign is required, and how is the downstream end normally marked?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The School Speed Limit assembly (or School Speed Limit When Flashing sign) must be placed at, or as near as practicable to, the point where the reduced school speed limit zone begins. In advance of the first such assembly in each direction, a School (S1-1) sign is required (using Table 2C-3 for advance placement). The downstream end of the zone normally must be marked with an END SCHOOL SPEED LIMIT (S5-3) sign, although an END SCHOOL ZONE (S5-2) sign may be substituted in certain circumstances. Standards (mandatory): - "A School Speed Limit assembly (see Figure 7B-1) or a School Speed Limit When Flashing (S5-1) sign (see Figure 7B-1) shall be used to indicate the speed limit where a reduced school speed limit zone has been established based upon an engineering study or where a reduced school speed limit is specified for such areas by statute. The School Speed Limit assembly or School Speed Limit When Flashing sign shall be placed at or as near as practicable to the point where the reduced school speed limit zone begins (see Figures 7B-2 and 7B-4)." - "If a reduced school speed limit zone has been established, a School (S1-1) sign shall be installed in advance (see Table 2C-3 for advance placement guidelines) of the first School Speed Limit sign assembly or S5-1 sign that is encountered in each direction as traffic approaches the reduced school speed limit zone (see Figures 7B-2 and 7B-4)." - "Except as provided in Paragraph 4 of this Section, the downstream end of an authorized and posted reduced school speed limit zone shall be identified with an END SCHOOL SPEED LIMIT (S5-3) sign (see Figures 7B-1, 7B-2, and 7B-4)." - "The static School Speed Limit assembly shall consist of a top plaque (S4-3P) with the legend SCHOOL, a Speed Limit (R2-1) sign, and a bottom plaque (S4-1P, S4-2P, S4-4P, or S4-6P) indicating the specific periods of the day and/or days of the week that the special school speed limit is in effect (see Figure 7B-1)." - "The School Speed Limit assembly shall be either a static sign assembly, a blank-out sign, or a changeable message sign (see Chapter 2L)." Options (permitted): - "The downstream end of a designated school zone may be identified with an END SCHOOL ZONE (S5-2) sign (see Figures 7B-1 and 7B-2)." Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 7B-2 shows the School (S1-1) sign installed in advance of the School Speed Limit assembly (S4-3P/R2-1/S4-1P) at the beginning of the zone, with END SCHOOL SPEED LIMIT (S5-3) or END SCHOOL ZONE (S5-2) signs marking the downstream end in each direction. - [Image 2] Figure 7B-4 similarly shows the S1-1 sign preceding the School Speed Limit assembly and the S5-3 (or S5-2) sign at the downstream end of the reduced school speed limit zone with higher fines plaques. - [Image 3] Figure 7B-1 illustrates the composition of the School Speed Limit assembly (S4-3P SCHOOL plaque, R2-1 Speed Limit sign, and S4-1P/S4-2P/S4-4P/S4-6P bottom plaques) as well as the S5-2 and S5-3 end-of-zone signs. Citations: - Section 7B.05 Standard §1 (p.978) - Section 7B.05 Standard §2 (p.978) - Section 7B.05 Standard §3 (p.978) - Section 7B.05 Standard §7 (p.980) - Section 7B.05 Standard §6 (p.980) - Section 7B.02 Option §7 (p.976) - Figure 7B-2 (p.975) - Figure 7B-4 (p.979) - Figure 7B-1 (p.973)
gold_answer: The assembly or S5-1 sign must be at or as near as practicable to the point where the reduced zone begins. A School (S1-1) sign must be placed in advance of the first school-speed-limit sign in each direction. The downstream end is normally marked with an END SCHOOL SPEED LIMIT (S5-3) sign, with an END SCHOOL ZONE (S5-2) allowed when the two zones end together.
